quick: 200 mg PO three times daily (600 mg/day)
summary: Oxaceprol is a hydroxyproline derivative (N-acetyl-4-hydroxy-L-proline) used in some European and Asian markets as a symptomatic anti-inflammatory and chondroprotective agent for osteoarthritis. It is not FDA-approved. The usual dose is 200 mg three times daily. It is generally well tolerated with mainly mild gastrointestinal effects, lacking the typical NSAID gastric and renal toxicity profile.
indications: Symptomatic treatment of degenerative joint disease (osteoarthritis) of the knee, hip and other joints
Adjunct management of joint pain and stiffness in osteoarthritis

dosage.d: 200 mg two to three times daily based on response

admin: Take tablets orally with or after meals to minimize gastrointestinal upset
Swallow whole with water; maintain regular dosing for symptomatic benefit
Reassess after several weeks; discontinue if no benefit
Use as a symptomatic adjunct alongside non-pharmacologic osteoarthritis measures
Follow the specific national product labeling for exact dosing
moa: Oxaceprol is an N-acetylated derivative of hydroxyproline, a key amino acid of collagen. It exerts anti-inflammatory activity by interfering with leukocyte adhesion and migration into inflamed tissue (reducing rolling and adhesion of leukocytes to endothelium) rather than through cyclooxygenase inhibition, and may support cartilage matrix, conferring a chondroprotective/symptomatic effect in osteoarthritis. The precise mechanism is not fully established.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to oxaceprol or excipients
relative: Severe renal or hepatic impairment (limited data)

preg: Safety in pregnancy has not been established; avoid use during pregnancy unless clearly necessary and no safer alternative exists.
lact: Safety during breastfeeding has not been established; avoid use or discontinue breastfeeding during therapy.
renal: Limited data; use with caution in renal impairment and consider monitoring, though oxaceprol lacks the typical NSAID renal toxicity.
hepatic: Limited data; use with caution in hepatic impairment.

moderate: No clinically significant interactions are well characterized; caution with other anti-inflammatory agents
interactions.food: May be taken with food to improve gastric tolerance.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction documented; general moderation advised.
interactions.diagnostics: No significant effect on laboratory tests documented.

monitoring: Symptomatic improvement in joint pain and function
Signs of hypersensitivity or skin reaction
counsel: Take with or after meals to reduce stomach upset
Benefit is symptomatic and may take some weeks; continue as directed
Combine with appropriate exercise, weight management and joint protection
Report any rash, swelling or persistent stomach upset
Inform your clinician of all other medicines and supplements you take
pk: Symptomatic effect over days to weeks
Oral absorption rapid; peak within ~1-2 hours
Short (a few hours); supports three-times-daily dosing
Store at room temperature, protected from moisture
pearls: NOTE: Oxaceprol is NOT FDA-approved; information is based on EMA/national SmPC and clinical literature (marketed e.g. as Jonctum/AHP-200 in some EU and Asian markets)
Acts by inhibiting leukocyte adhesion/migration rather than COX - lacks classic NSAID gastric and renal toxicity
Positioned as a well-tolerated symptomatic/chondroprotective option in osteoarthritis
Evidence base is more limited than for established NSAIDs
Reassess benefit after a few weeks and discontinue if ineffective
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it and resume the regular schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: No specific antidote. Overdose is expected to cause primarily gastrointestinal symptoms; manage with supportive and symptomatic care and gastric decontamination if a large recent ingestion.
